newsitem.title: USA: Helfer leaves FDIC, vice chair Hove takes reins.
newsitem.headline: Helfer leaves FDIC, vice chair Hove takes reins.

text.p: Andrew Hove became acting chairman of the Federal Deposit Insurance Corp on June 1, the agency said on Monday.
As expected, Hove succeeded Ricki Helfer, who announced in a letter to President Bill Clinton in March that she would resign her post at the beginning of June.
Previously vice chairman of the FDIC, 62-year-old Hove joined the agency in 1990. He twice served as acting chairman in the past, including for two years following the death of William Taylor.
President Clinton has not announced a nomination for a permanent replacement for Helfer.
